history.summary: The 'Thakurani Temple' row best matches the Maa Budhi Thakurani Temple near the Big Bazaar area (Desi Behera Street) in Berhampur (Brahmapur), Ganjam district, Odisha - the city's guardian deity and cultural cornerstone. Per local historians the cult originated with the Telugu-speaking Dera (Devangiri) weaver community, which migrated to Mahuri at the invitation of the Raja of Mahuri around 1672 AD and installed the goddess as the city's ista devi; priests are traditionally barbers (Nari/Barik community), a rare arrangement bridging caste lines (verify details). The famous biennial Thakurani Yatra (Ghata Yatra) in Chaitra celebrates the goddess as a married daughter visiting her parental home (the Desi Behera's house) for nearly a month. Note: generic 'Thakurani Temple' listings also exist in Berhampur localities such as Gosaninuagam and Triveni Nagar (Justdial entries) - the Budhi Thakurani Temple is the prominent referent; the CSV may conflate these (verify on the ground). Opening hours conflict across sources: 5:00 AM-9:00 PM (travelsetu) vs 5:45 AM-12:00 PM / 5:00 PM-9:00 PM (bloggymaster) - verify. No CSV correction: town Berhampur and district Ganjam are correct. Coordinates are the Big Bazaar area (verify exact temple point).
